D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The available catalogues label some actions read or modifying, but no official tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) or authenticated manifest were available. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter, preview flow, elicitation, or approval workflow was documented; catalogue instructions recommend explicit user intent for selected actions. 3. OAuth scopes are listed in the supplied resource metadata. Whether product roles or admin controls further constrain this endpoint is unknown. The metadata does not list token lifetime; it does list a revocation endpoint. 4. No official read-only mode, tool filters, query-free mode, sandbox, or regional variants were documented. A separate /chatgpt-mcp path returned 401; its purpose is unknown. 5. Catalogue instructions say to replace usernames/PII with “me/my” for search queries; no server-enforced masking was established. Spotify’s privacy policy includes searches, listening history, playlists, library, third-party app use, and AI-feature prompts among usage data. 6. Agent Discoverability descriptions mention limits of 20 entity URIs, 10 catalog lookups, 100 playlist items, search results up to 20 (10 default), and polling up to five times for pending generated playlists. These are catalogue statements; endpoint enforcement was not verified. Endpoint-specific rates and costs are unknown. 7. No official code or parameter-validation behavior was available. 8. No endpoint-specific logging or audit trail promise was found. 9. Search of the reported action names and descriptions found no feedback, rating, survey, or report tool. No endpoint-specific upsell result was observed; some catalogue text describes Premium prerequisites. 10. Third-party catalogue descriptions contain behavioral rules, but enforcement by Spotify’s server is unknown; no server-delivered skill was documented. 11. Spotify’s own recommendation systems use a taste profile influenced by activity, but whether MCP calls alter future MCP outputs beyond ordinary account changes is unknown. 12. The endpoint is presented as Spotify’s hosted server. No sub-server hierarchy was documented. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, script, or general execution tool appears in the reported tool sets.

E_aggregated.action_count: 15 distinct names across catalogues; 13 reported by Agent Discoverability and six by other listings
E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official Spotify tool list for this consumer endpoint was found in the prepared pages, their scripts/HTML, or official documentation. Claude’s connector directory lists six names for this endpoint (third-party listing, despite identifying Spotify as the publisher). Agent Discoverability lists 13 names for its ChatGPT plugin profile tied to this endpoint. Tedix and Manufact each list six, matching the Claude names except for Remove_from_library capitalization in related listings. The union has 15 distinct strings because Agent Discoverability reports remove_from_library while the Claude directory reports Remove_from_library. No official total was found. No proxy-only tools were added. Composio’s Spotify toolkit describes a separate integration surface and was excluded.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim official tool definitions plus initialize instructions were available; catalogues do not provide a complete official manifest.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Spotify’s ChatGPT app page advertises conversational music and podcast discovery, playlist creation/editing, and playback handoff. The reported MCP tools do not document every feature or expose the full Spotify app interface. Official Spotify Web API references cover many additional endpoints, but REST-only operations cannot be assumed to be available through this MCP endpoint. The official Spotify Ads API guide also identifies UI functions such as user management and billing/payment as unsupported by that separate Ads API; that is not evidence about this consumer server.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: No official endpoint-specific behavioral guidance was found. Third-party Agent Discoverability descriptions advise explicit intent for playlist creation/removal, recommend using search instead of playlist generation for discovery requests, and prescribe language and link handling. These instructions’ enforcement by Spotify’s server is unknown.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Spotify’s privacy policy applies to connecting a Spotify account with another application and lists searches, streaming history, playlists, library, third-party services, and AI-feature prompts among usage data. It states that personal data entered as search queries is deleted after 90 days, subject to other retention rules. Spotify’s recommendation explanation says recommendations are personalized using taste profile and activity, and describes Discovery Mode as a commercial signal that can increase recommendation likelihood.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Spotify’s ChatGPT page describes personalized music and podcast suggestions based on history, favorite artists, and listening patterns, with the option to disconnect in Settings. Its recommendation explainer states that recommendations reflect user taste and that commercial considerations can sometimes influence recommendations.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The supplied OAuth metadata establishes an authorization boundary and scopes. No public server code or official endpoint documentation was found to verify enforcement of privacy, retention, query handling, personalization, or commercial recommendation statements at the MCP layer.

contradictions: The Claude connector directory, Tedix, and Manufact report six tools, while Agent Discoverability reports 13 tools for the same endpoint’s ChatGPT profile. No official list was found to resolve whether this reflects different client surfaces or catalogue versions.

The Claude connector directory spells the library-removal tool Remove_from_library, while Agent Discoverability lists remove_from_library. They are recorded as separate exact names because no official manifest was available to establish whether one supersedes the other.

Integrations.sh describes the endpoint as requiring a preregistered OAuth app and says DCR/CIMD are unsupported. The supplied OAuth metadata contains no registration_endpoint, but does not itself explicitly state that registration is unsupported.

Manufact’s page claims the endpoint does not require authentication, while the supplied endpoint check returned HTTP 401 and supplied protected-resource metadata advertises OAuth. The direct endpoint evidence contradicts that catalogue claim.

Manufact describes the endpoint as a public endpoint with no authentication, but its own page also reports failed connection due to authentication required. The catalogue statements conflict internally and with the supplied 401 evidence.
observations_for_research: A single global endpoint is associated with differently sized tool inventories in third-party records: six tools for one connector listing and 13 for a ChatGPT plugin profile. The available evidence does not establish whether the difference is client-specific, version-specific, or catalogue drift.

Several detailed tool instructions are visible only in the third-party ChatGPT profile. The authenticated Spotify manifest could not be inspected to compare those descriptions with server-delivered tool metadata.
